title: Ensure pg_hba.conf does not use 'trust' or 'password' authentication
description: trust allows login without any credential and password sends the password in clear text. The CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark covers pg_hba.conf only through the manual checks 5.3/5.4; this rule automates that part by reading pg_hba_file_rules (superuser). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 / 5.4 Ensure login via "local" UNIX Domain Socket / "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE auth_method IN ('trust','password')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Replace trust/password entries in pg_hba.conf with scram-sha-256 (or peer for local administrative sockets), then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure Data Cluster Initialized Successfully
description: First-time installs of a given PostgreSQL major release require the instantiation of the database cluster. A database cluster is a collection of databases that are managed by a single server instance. Checks that data_directory holds an initialized cluster (PG_VERSION) owned by postgres with mode 0700 or 0750; run on the database host. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure Data Cluster Initialized Successfully

audit.command: d=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW data_directory" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -f "$d/PG_VERSION" ] || { echo "no PG_VERSION in $d"; exit 0; }; s=$(stat -c '%a %U' "$d" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; case "$s" in "700 postgres"|"750 postgres") echo compliant ;; *) echo "$s" ;; esac

remediation.command: Initialize the cluster with checksums (PGSETUP_INITDB_OPTIONS="-k" postgresql-18-setup initdb, or initdb -k) and ensure the data directory is owned by postgres with mode 0700 (0750 with group access): chown postgres:postgres <data_directory>; chmod 0700 <data_directory>.

title: Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied
description: PostgreSQL updates are released to resolve bugs, and mitigate vulnerabilities quarterly (or sooner for drastic CVEs). It is recommended that PostgreSQL installations are kept up to date with the latest security updates.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure the Latest Security Patches are Applied

audit.command: Run SHOW server_version; and compare the result with the latest minor release and the security announcements on https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/ (and your OS vendor advisories if using distro packages). A server that is not on the latest minor release of its major version is a fail.

remediation.command: Apply the latest minor release with the package manager (dnf update postgresql18* / apt upgrade postgresql-18) during a maintenance window, then restart PostgreSQL.

title: Ensure extension directory has appropriate ownership and permissions
description: The extension directory is the location of the PostgreSQL extensions. Extensions are storage engines or user defined functions (UDFs). Reads SHAREDIR from the pg_config view (superuser) and requires <sharedir>/extension to be drwxr-xr-x root:root. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure extension directory has appropriate ownership and permissions

audit.command: sd=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT setting FROM pg_config WHERE name = 'SHAREDIR'" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ -n "$sd" ] || exit 1; s=$(stat -c '%a %U %G' "$sd/extension" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; [ "$s" = "755 root root" ] && echo compliant || echo "$s"

remediation.command: chown root:root <sharedir>/extension && chmod 0755 <sharedir>/extension (sharedir from pg_config --sharedir). If the permissions needed correcting, verify that no extension files in that directory were modified.

title: Ensure the PostgreSQL Audit Extension (pgAudit) is enabled
description: The PostgreSQL Audit Extension (pgAudit) provides detailed session and/or object audit logging via the standard PostgreSQL logging facility. The goal of pgAudit is to provide PostgreSQL users with the capability to produce audit logs often required to comply with government, financial, or ISO certifications. Passes when pgaudit is in shared_preload_libraries and pgaudit.log selects at least one class. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure the PostgreSQL Audit Extension (pgAudit) is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN 'pgaudit' = ANY (string_to_array(replace(current_setting('shared_preload_libraries'), ' ', ''), ',')) AND coalesce(current_setting('pgaudit.log', true), '') NOT IN ('', 'none') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Install pgAudit (dnf install pgaudit_18 / apt install postgresql-18-pgaudit), add pgaudit to shared_preload_libraries (keep existing entries), set pgaudit.log (e.g. 'ddl,write') in postgresql.conf, restart PostgreSQL and run CREATE EXTENSION pgaudit;

title: Ensure excessive administrative privileges are revoked
description: With respect to PostgreSQL administrative SQL commands, only superusers should have elevated privileges. PostgreSQL regular, or application, users should not possess the ability to create roles, create new databases, manage replication, or perform any other action deemed privileged.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure excessive administrative privileges are revoked

audit.command: Run psql -c "\du+" and review role attributes (Superuser, Create role, Create DB, Replication, Bypass RLS). Only designated administrative roles may hold them; any regular role with administrative attributes is a fail.

remediation.command: Revoke unneeded attributes, e.g. ALTER ROLE <role> NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE NOCREATEDB NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS;

title: Ensure all accounts that can log in have passwords
description: If not using certificate-based authentication, all database accounts that have the ability to login should have a password set.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.10 Ensure all accounts that can log in have passwords

audit.command: Run SELECT rolname FROM pg_authid WHERE rolpassword IS NULL AND rolcanlogin; Any returned account that is not known to authenticate with certificates (or peer/GSS) is a potential fail.

remediation.command: Set a password for each listed account with \password <user> in psql (ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD writes the password to logs), or switch it to certificate authentication.

title: Ensure login via "local" UNIX Domain Socket is configured correctly
description: A remote host login, via SSH, is arguably the most secure means of remotely accessing and administering the PostgreSQL server. Once connected to the PostgreSQL server, using the psql client, via UNIX DOMAIN SOCKETS, while using the peer authentication method is the most secure mechanism available for local database connections.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure login via "local" UNIX Domain Socket is configured correctly

audit.command: Review the 'local' lines of pg_hba.conf (SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE type = 'local';). As user1 run psql -U postgres -d postgres: it must fail with 'Peer authentication failed'; as postgres it must succeed. Local login as another account than your own is a fail.

remediation.command: Use 'local all all peer' (or 'local all postgres peer') as the local rule, create database roles that match OS users that need access, then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure login via "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly
description: A large number of authentication METHODs are available for hosts connecting using TCP/IP sockets, including: ; trust ; reject ; md5 ; scram-sha-256 ; password ; gss ; sspi ; ident ; pam ; ldap ; radius ; cert ; oauth METHODs trust, password, and ident are not to be used for remote logins.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure login via "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly

audit.command: Review 'host' lines in pg_hba.conf (SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE type LIKE 'host%';). Test psql 'host=<server> user=postgres sslmode=disable' and sslmode=require locally and remotely: only intended encrypted, password-authenticated (scram-sha-256) logins may succeed.

remediation.command: Use hostssl lines with scram-sha-256 for required users/networks and hostnossl ... reject for the rest, e.g. hostssl all postgres 0.0.0.0/0 scram-sha-256 and hostnossl all postgres 0.0.0.0/0 reject, then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly
description: TLS on a PostgreSQL server should be enabled and configured to encrypt TCP traffic to and from the server. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.8 Ensure TLS is enabled and configured correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW ssl" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Install a CA-issued server certificate and key (key mode 0600, owned by postgres), set ssl = on, ssl_cert_file and ssl_key_file in postgresql.conf, then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure the TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 Protocols are Disabled
description: Transport Layer Security (TLS), and its predecessor Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) are cryptographic protocols which can be used to encrypt data sent between client and server. Passes for TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3 (preferred). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.9 Ensure the TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 Protocols are Disabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('ssl_min_protocol_version') IN ('TLSv1.2','TLSv1.3') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.3'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'password_encryption' is set to 'scram-sha-256'
description: New passwords should be stored as SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers rather than MD5 hashes (MD5 support is deprecated in PostgreSQL 18). Not a separate CIS PostgreSQL 18 recommendation (see the 5.4 default-value notes). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure login via "host" TCP/IP Socket is configured correctly (default value notes on password_encryption)

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW password_encryption" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure packages are obtained from authorized repositories
description: Standard Linux distributions, although possessing the requisite packages, often do not have PostgreSQL pre-installed. The installation process includes installing the binaries and the means to generate a data cluster. Package installation should include both the server and client packages.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure packages are obtained from authorized repositories

audit.command: List enabled package repositories (RHEL: dnf repolist all | grep -E 'enabled$'; Debian/Ubuntu: apt-cache policy) and confirm each is organization-approved (e.g. vendor OS repos or the PGDG repository). Inspect installed PostgreSQL packages (rpm -qa | grep postgres or dpkg -l | grep postgres) and confirm they come from those sources. Any unapproved repository is a fail.

remediation.command: Disable or remove unapproved repositories and reinstall PostgreSQL packages from an authorized source (OS vendor or PGDG).

title: Verify That 'PGPASSWORD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles
description: PostgreSQL can read a default database password from an environment variable called PGPASSWORD. Run as root; counts Bash login scripts in /home/*, /root and /etc/environment that mention PGPASSWORD (other shells need manual review).
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Verify That 'PGPASSWORD' is Not Set in Users' Profiles

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -ls PGPASSWORD /home/*/.bashrc /home/*/.profile /home/*/.bash_profile /root/.bashrc /root/.profile /root/.bash_profile /etc/environment 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Remove PGPASSWORD from the listed login scripts and use ~/.pgpass (mode 0600), a service file without passwords, or certificate/peer authentication instead.

title: Verify That the 'PGPASSWORD' Environment Variable is Not in Use
description: PostgreSQL can read a default database password from an environment variable called PGPASSWORD. Run as root; counts processes whose environment contains PGPASSWORD (including the scanner itself if it was given PGPASSWORD).
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Verify That the 'PGPASSWORD' Environment Variable is Not in Use

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; n=$(grep -lsaz '^PGPASSWORD=' /proc/[0-9]*/environ 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "$n"

remediation.command: Find the processes (grep -lsaz ^PGPASSWORD= /proc/*/environ) and change the users or scripts that export PGPASSWORD to use ~/.pgpass or another secure method.

title: Ensure the file permissions mask is correct
description: Files are always created using a default set of permissions. File permissions can be restricted by applying a permissions mask called the umask. The postgres user account should use a umask of 0077 to deny file access to all user accounts except the owner.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure the file permissions mask is correct

audit.command: As root run su - postgres -c umask. The umask must be 0077 or more restrictive for the postgres user (check .bash_profile, .profile and .bashrc of the postgres home); otherwise this is a fail.

remediation.command: As postgres add 'umask 077' to the profile file in use (e.g. ~postgres/.bash_profile) and re-login to confirm umask prints 0077.

title: Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the service file
description: One can set a password in a PostgreSQL connection service file. Verify the password option is not used in a connection service file.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure Passwords are Not Stored in the service file

audit.command: As root search connection service files for passwords: find / -name .pg_service.conf -type f -exec grep -H password {} \; 2>/dev/null; grep password /root/.pg_service.conf "${PGSERVICEFILE}" "${PGSYSCONFDIR}/pg_service.conf". Any password=... line is a finding.

remediation.command: Remove password= entries from pg_service.conf/.pg_service.conf files and store credentials in ~/.pgpass (mode 0600) or use certificate authentication.

title: Ensure the logging collector is enabled
description: The logging collector is a background process that captures log messages sent to stderr and redirects them into log files. The logging_collector setting must be enabled in order for this process to run. It can only be set at the server start. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.3 Ensure the logging collector is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW logging_collector" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET logging_collector = 'on'; then restart PostgreSQL (systemctl restart postgresql-18); this parameter only changes at server start.

title: Ensure the log file permissions are set correctly
description: The log_file_mode setting determines the file permissions for log files when logging_collector is enabled. The parameter value is expected to be a numeric mode specification in the form accepted by the chmod and umask system calls. Expects 0600, the benchmark value and default. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.6 Ensure the log file permissions are set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW log_file_mode" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_file_mode = '0600'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure the correct messages are written to the server log
description: The log_min_messages setting specifies the message levels that are written to the server log. Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The lower the level (vertically, below), the fewer messages are logged. Passes when log_min_messages is warning or a more verbose level. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.14 Ensure the correct messages are written to the server log

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN lower(current_setting('log_min_messages')) IN ('debug5','debug4','debug3','debug2','debug1','info','notice','warning') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_min_messages = 'warning'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure the correct SQL statements generating errors are recorded
description: The log_min_error_statement setting causes all SQL statements generating errors at or above the specified severity level to be recorded in the server log. Each level includes all the levels that follow it. The lower the level (vertically, below), the fewer messages are recorded. Passes when log_min_error_statement is error or a more verbose level. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.15 Ensure the correct SQL statements generating errors are recorded

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN lower(current_setting('log_min_error_statement')) IN ('debug5','debug4','debug3','debug2','debug1','info','notice','warning','error') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_min_error_statement = 'error'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_connections' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_connections setting causes each attempted connection to the server to be logged, as well as successful completion of client authentication. This parameter cannot be changed after the session start. PostgreSQL 18 turned log_connections into a list; 'all' (or receipt,authentication,authorization,setup_durations) passes, the pre-18 boolean 'on' does not. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.20 Ensure 'log_connections' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('log_connections') = 'all' OR string_to_array(replace(current_setting('log_connections'), ' ', ''), ',') @> ARRAY['receipt','authentication','authorization','setup_durations'] THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_connections = 'all'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_disconnections' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_disconnections setting logs the end of each session, including session duration. This parameter cannot be changed after the session start. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.21 Ensure 'log_disconnections' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW log_disconnections" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_disconnections = 'on'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_line_prefix' is set correctly
description: The log_line_prefix setting specifies a printf-style string that is prefixed to each log line. If blank, no prefix is used. You should configure this as recommended by the pgBadger development team unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy. % characters begin "escape sequences" that are replaced with status information as outlined below. Requires the escapes %m %p %l %d %u %a %h (only %d %u %a %h when log_destination is syslog alone). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.24 Ensure 'log_line_prefix' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT (d = 'syslog' OR (strpos(s, '%m') > 0 AND strpos(s, '%p') > 0 AND strpos(s, '%l') > 0)) AND strpos(s, '%d') > 0 AND strpos(s, '%u') > 0 AND strpos(s, '%a') > 0 AND strpos(s, '%h') > 0 FROM (SELECT current_setting('log_line_prefix') AS s, replace(current_setting('log_destination'), ' ', '') AS d) x) THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_line_prefix = '%m [%p]: [%l-1] db=%d,user=%u,app=%a,client=%h '" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_statement' is set correctly
description: The log_statement setting specifies the types of SQL statements that are logged. Valid values are: ; none (off) ; ddl ; mod ; all (all statements) It is recommended this be set to ddl unless otherwise directed by your organization's logging policy. Fails only when log_statement is none; choose ddl, mod or all per policy. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.25 Ensure 'log_statement' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('log_statement') <> 'none' THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_statement = 'ddl'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled
description: When created, the PostgreSQL user may have interactive access to the operating system, which means that the PostgreSQL user could login to the host as any other user would.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure Interactive Login is Disabled

audit.command: Run sudo grep postgres /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f1-2. Unless the output is postgres:!<something> (locked password), interactive login is possible and this is a fail.

remediation.command: Lock the account password: passwd -l postgres (and optionally set its shell to /sbin/nologin if no one uses sudo -iu postgres). Administrators then use sudo -iu postgres.

title: Ensure sudo is configured correctly
description: It is common to have more than one authorized individual administering the PostgreSQL service at the Operating System level. It is also quite common to permit login privileges to individuals on a PostgreSQL host who otherwise are not authorized to access the server's data cluster and files.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure sudo is configured correctly

audit.command: Check /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d: only an approved DBA group (e.g. %dba) may run commands as postgres. Test with an unauthorized user (sudo -iu postgres must be refused) and an authorized one.

remediation.command: Create a DBA group, add authorized users, and add '%dba ALL=(postgres) PASSWD: ALL' via visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/postgres.

title: Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use
description: If users with database accounts will not be using the database for some time, disabling the account will reduce the risk of attacks or inappropriate account usage.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Lock Out Accounts if Not Currently in Use

audit.command: Run SELECT rolname FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname !~ '^pg_' AND rolcanlogin; and compare with the accounts currently in use. Inactive accounts must not appear in the output.

remediation.command: Lock unused accounts with ALTER ROLE <role> NOLOGIN; (re-enable with LOGIN when needed) or drop them.

title: Ensure excessive function privileges are revoked
description: In certain situations, to provide the required functionality, PostgreSQL needs to execute internal logic (stored procedures, functions, triggers, etc.) and/or external code modules with elevated privileges. Counts SECURITY DEFINER functions outside pg_catalog/information_schema that are not owned by an extension, in the database it connects to (set PGDATABASE to check each database); accept justified functions as exceptions. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure excessive function privileges are revoked

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace WHERE p.prosecdef AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND p.proname NOT LIKE 'pgaudit%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_depend d WHERE d.classid = 'pg_proc'::regclass AND d.objid = p.oid AND d.deptype = 'e')" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Review each SECURITY DEFINER function; switch it with ALTER FUNCTION <name>(<args>) SECURITY INVOKER; or, if elevation is required, REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION <name>(<args>) FROM PUBLIC/<roles> so only the accounts that need it can run it.

title: Ensure excessive DML privileges are revoked
description: DML (insert, update, delete) operations at the table level should be restricted to only authorized users. PostgreSQL manages table-level DML permissions via the GRANT statement.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.6 Ensure excessive DML privileges are revoked

audit.command: In each database list roles (\du+ *) and tables (\dt *.*), then review grants, e.g. SELECT grantee, table_schema, table_name, privilege_type FROM information_schema.role_table_grants WHERE grantee NOT IN ('postgres','PUBLIC'); Any INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE grant a role does not need is a fail.

remediation.command: REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON <schema>.<table> FROM <role>; for each excessive grant, keeping only what the role requires.

title: Ensure Row Level Security (RLS) is configured correctly
description: In addition to the SQL-standard privilege system available through GRANT, tables can have row security policies that restrict, on a per-user basis, which individual rows can be returned by normal queries or inserted, updated, or deleted by data modification commands. This feature is also known as Row Level Security (RLS).
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.7 Ensure Row Level Security (RLS) is configured correctly

audit.command: Determine which tables need row level security, then run SELECT oid, relname, relrowsecurity FROM pg_class WHERE relrowsecurity IS TRUE; Any table that requires RLS but is missing from the result (or lacks policies, see \d+ <table>) is a fail.

remediation.command: ALTER TABLE <table> ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; then CREATE POLICY ... for each required access rule, and confirm roles that must obey RLS do not have BYPASSRLS.

title: Ensure the set_user extension is installed
description: PostgreSQL access to the superuser database role must be controlled and audited to prevent unauthorized access. Note: Prior to performing this audit you must create a roletree view. Passes when set_user is available and no login role is a superuser directly or through role membership (the benchmark sets postgres NOLOGIN; then run the scan with PGUSER set to a DBA role). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.8 Ensure the set_user extension is installed

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'set_user') AND NOT EXISTS (WITH RECURSIVE m(member, roleid) AS (SELECT member, roleid FROM pg_auth_members UNION SELECT m.member, a.roleid FROM m JOIN pg_auth_members a ON a.member = m.roleid) SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles r WHERE r.rolcanlogin AND (r.rolsuper OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM m JOIN pg_roles s ON s.oid = m.roleid WHERE m.member = r.oid AND s.rolsuper))) THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Install set_user (dnf install set_user_18), add set_user to shared_preload_libraries, restart, CREATE EXTENSION set_user; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION set_user(text) to DBA login roles, then ALTER ROLE postgres NOLOGIN; and remove SUPERUSER/LOGIN or superuser role memberships from other login roles.

title: Make use of predefined roles
description: PostgreSQL provides a set of predefined roles that provide access to certain commonly needed privileged capabilities and information. Administrators can GRANT these roles to users and/or other roles in their environment, providing those users with access to the specified capabilities and information.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.9 Make use of predefined roles

audit.command: Run SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper IS TRUE; and, for each superuser other than the bootstrap account, decide whether predefined roles (pg_read_all_data, pg_write_all_data, pg_monitor, pg_signal_backend, pg_checkpoint, pg_maintain, ...) would suffice. Unneeded superusers are a fail.

remediation.command: GRANT the suitable predefined role(s) to the account, then ALTER ROLE <role> NOSUPERUSER;

title: Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line
description: When a command is executed on the command line, for example ; psql postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@host the password may be visible in the user's shell/command history or in the process list, thus exposing the password to other entities on the server.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Do Not Specify Passwords in the Command Line

audit.command: Check the process list (sudo ps -few) and shell histories (history, ~/.bash_history) for psql/pg_dump invocations that contain a password, e.g. in a connection string (password=...). Any visible password is a fail.

remediation.command: Do not pass passwords on the command line; use ~/.pgpass (mode 0600), a service file without passwords, or certificate authentication, and clear exposed history entries.

title: Ensure PostgreSQL is Bound to an IP Address
description: By default, listen_addresses is set to localhost which prevents any and all remote TCP connections to the PostgreSQL port. Some Docker images may set listen_addesses to *. * corresponds to all available IP interfaces; thus, the PostgreSQL server then accepts TCP connections on all the server's IPv6 and IPv4 interfaces.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure PostgreSQL is Bound to an IP Address

audit.command: Run SHOW listen_addresses; If * or 0.0.0.0 is returned, PostgreSQL listens on every interface and this is a fail.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET listen_addresses = 'localhost,<specific IP>'; (or set it in postgresql.conf) and restart PostgreSQL.

title: Ensure Password Complexity is configured
description: Password complexity configuration is crucial to restrict unauthorized access to data. By default, PostgreSQL doesn't provide for password complexity. Moreover, many compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS, and HIPPA require both password complexity and length.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.6 Ensure Password Complexity is configured

audit.command: Run SHOW shared_preload_libraries; and SHOW dynamic_library_path; If $libdir/passwordcheck (or passwordcheck when dynamic_library_path is $libdir) is not listed in shared_preload_libraries, this is a failure.

remediation.command: Add '$libdir/passwordcheck' to shared_preload_libraries in postgresql.conf (keep existing entries), optionally set passwordcheck.min_password_length, and restart PostgreSQL.

title: Ensure 'backend' runtime parameters are configured correctly
description: In order to serve multiple clients efficiently, the PostgreSQL server launches a new "backend" process for each client. The runtime parameters in this benchmark section are controlled by the backend process. Checks the benchmark's expected backend values ignore_system_indexes=off, jit_debugging_support=off, jit_profiling_support=off and post_auth_delay=0 (log_connections/log_disconnections are 3.1.20/3.1.21). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure 'backend' runtime parameters are configured correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_settings WHERE (name, setting) IN (('ignore_system_indexes','off'),('jit_debugging_support','off'),('jit_profiling_support','off'),('post_auth_delay','0'))) = 4 THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: Correct unauthorized backend parameters in postgresql.conf/postgresql.auto.conf (or the pg_ctl command line / $PGDATA/postmaster.opts) and restart PostgreSQL; compare SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE context IN ('backend','superuser-backend') with your baseline.

title: Ensure FIPS 140-2 OpenSSL Cryptography Is Used
description: Install, configure, and use OpenSSL on a platform that has a NIST certified FIPS 140-2 installation of OpenSSL. This provides PostgreSQL instances the ability to generate and validate cryptographic hashes to protect unclassified information requiring confidentiality and cryptographic protection, in accordance with the data owner's requirements. Requires kernel FIPS mode (/proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled = 1) and an active OpenSSL FIPS provider; the benchmark notes this is natively possible only on RHEL-family systems.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.7 Ensure FIPS 140-2 OpenSSL Cryptography Is Used

audit.command: f=$(cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; p=$(openssl list -providers 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ "$f" = 1 ] && printf '%s\n' "$p" | grep -qi fips; then echo compliant; else echo noncompliant; fi

remediation.command: Enable FIPS mode on a FIPS-capable OS (RHEL/Rocky: fips-mode-setup --enable, then reboot) so OpenSSL, which PostgreSQL uses, runs with the FIPS provider; confirm with fips-mode-setup --check.

title: Ensure Weak SSL/TLS Ciphers Are Disabled
description: The PostgreSQL ssl_ciphers and ssl_tls13_ciphers directives specify which Cipher Suites are allowed in the negotiation with the client. ssl_ciphers is used to specify the list of allowed cipher suites for TLS 1.2 and earlier versions. While ssl_tls13_ciphers is a list of cipher suites that are allowed by connections using TLS version 1.3. Passes only when ssl_ciphers and ssl_tls13_ciphers (PostgreSQL 18) list nothing but TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256; an empty ssl_tls13_ciphers falls back to the OpenSSL defaults and fails. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.10 Ensure Weak SSL/TLS Ciphers Are Disabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM regexp_split_to_table(current_setting('ssl_ciphers') || ':' || coalesce(current_setting('ssl_tls13_ciphers', true), ''), '[:,]') AS t(c) WHERE btrim(c) NOT IN ('TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384','TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256','TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256')) THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.guidance: ALTER SYSTEM SET ssl_ciphers = 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256'; ALTER SYSTEM SET ssl_tls13_ciphers = 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256,TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256'; SELECT pg_reload_conf(); then check pg_stat_ssl for sessions using other ciphers.

title: Ensure a replication-only user is created and used for streaming replication
description: Create a new user specifically for use by streaming replication instead of using the superuser account.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.1 Ensure a replication-only user is created and used for streaming replication

audit.command: Run SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolreplication IS TRUE; Streaming replication must use a dedicated, non-superuser role with only the REPLICATION attribute; replication via postgres or another superuser is a fail.

remediation.command: CREATE ROLE replication_user WITH LOGIN REPLICATION PASSWORD '<pw>'; and add a 'hostssl replication replication_user <standby_ip>/32 scram-sha-256' line to pg_hba.conf, then reload.

title: Ensure base backups are configured and functional
description: A 'base backup' is a copy of the PRIMARY host's data cluster ($PGDATA) and is used to create STANDBY hosts and for Point In Time Recovery (PITR) mechanisms. Base backups should be copied across networks in a secure manner using an encrypted transport mechanism.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.3 Ensure base backups are configured and functional

audit.command: Confirm that base backups (pg_basebackup, pgBackRest or similar) exist, are taken on a regular schedule, are stored off-host, and that restores are tested.

remediation.command: Schedule regular base backups (e.g. pg_basebackup -D <dir> -Ft -z -P or pgBackRest), store them separately from the database server with restricted access, and test restores.

title: Ensure WAL archiving is configured and functional
description: Write Ahead Log (WAL) Archiving, or Log Shipping, is the process of sending transaction log files from the PRIMARY host either to one or more STANDBY hosts or to be archived on a remote storage device for later use, e.g. PITR. There are several utilities that can copy WALs including, but not limited to, cp, scp, sftp, and rynsc. Passes when archive_mode is on/always and archive_command or archive_library is set; also confirm pg_stat_archiver shows successful archiving. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.4 Ensure WAL archiving is configured and functional

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('archive_mode') IN ('on','always') AND (current_setting('archive_command') NOT IN ('', '(disabled)') OR current_setting('archive_library') <> '') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: Set archive_mode = on and archive_command (e.g. 'pgbackrest --stanza=<name> archive-push %p') or archive_library in postgresql.conf, restart PostgreSQL, then confirm archived_count grows and failed_count stays constant in pg_stat_archiver.

title: Ensure streaming replication parameters are configured correctly
description: Streaming replication from a PRIMARY host transmits DDL, DML, passwords, and other potentially sensitive activities and data. These connections should be protected with Secure Sockets Layer (SSL).
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.5 Ensure streaming replication parameters are configured correctly

audit.command: Confirm a dedicated non-superuser replication role exists (SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolreplication;) and, from the standby, that psql 'host=<primary> dbname=postgres user=replication_user sslmode=require' -c 'select 1;' succeeds; check primary_conninfo on the standby uses sslmode=require or stronger.

remediation.command: On the standby set primary_conninfo = 'host=<primary> user=replication_user sslmode=verify-full ...' (and primary_slot_name), create standby.signal, and allow only hostssl replication entries on the primary.

title: Install only required packages
description: Depending on the distribution, several other packages next to the mandatory postgresql might have been installed upon a system. Typical add-on packages are: ; postgresql-doc: PostgreSQL documentation. ; phppgadmin: PostgreSQL web-based administration tool. ; ...
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Install only required packages

audit.command: List installed PostgreSQL packages (rpm -qa | grep -i postgres or dpkg -l | grep -i postgres) and compare with apt search postgresql / dnf search postgresql. Only packages required for this server's role (server, client, needed contrib/extensions) should be installed; anything unneeded is a finding.

remediation.command: Remove PostgreSQL packages and extensions not required for the server role with the OS package manager (dnf remove / apt remove).

title: Ensure systemd Service Files Are Enabled
description: Confirm, and correct if necessary, the PostgreSQL systemd service is enabled. Passes when at least one postgresql* systemd service unit is enabled.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure systemd Service Files Are Enabled

audit.command: out=$(systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --no-legend 'postgresql*' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2=="enabled"{e=1} END{print e?"enabled":"not-enabled"}'

remediation.command: Enable the PostgreSQL unit for the default target, e.g. systemctl enable postgresql-18 (PGDG) or systemctl enable postgresql (Debian/Ubuntu), then confirm with systemctl is-enabled.

title: Disable PostgreSQL Command History
description: On Linux/UNIX, the PostgreSQL client logs most interactive statements to a history file. The default PostgreSQL history file is named .psql_history in the user's home directory. The PostgreSQL command history should be disabled. Run as root; counts .psql_history files under /home, /root and the postgres home that are not symlinks to /dev/null.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Disable PostgreSQL Command History

audit.command: [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || exit 1; h=$(getent passwd postgres | cut -d: -f6); l=$(find /home /root $h -maxdepth 3 -name .psql_history 2>/dev/null); n=0; for f in $l; do [ "$(readlink "$f")" = /dev/null ] || n=$((n+1)); done; echo "$n"

remediation.command: For each user: rm -f ~<user>/.psql_history, then either add '\set HISTFILE /dev/null' to ~<user>/.psqlrc or ln -s /dev/null ~<user>/.psql_history; optionally set PSQL_HISTORY=/dev/null in /etc/environment.

title: Ensure the log destinations are set correctly
description: PostgreSQL supports several methods for logging server messages, including stderr, csvlog, syslog, and jsonlog. On Windows, eventlog is also supported. One or more of these destinations should be set for server log output.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.2 Ensure the log destinations are set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_destination; (default stderr) and confirm it contains every destination required by your logging policy (stderr, csvlog, jsonlog, syslog, eventlog). Missing required destinations are a fail.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_destination = 'csvlog'; (or a comma-separated list such as 'csvlog, syslog') then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure the log file destination directory is set correctly
description: The log_directory setting specifies the destination directory for log files when log_destination is stderr or csvlog. It can be specified as relative to the cluster data directory ($PGDATA) or as an absolute path. log_directory should be set according to your organization's logging policy.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.4 Ensure the log file destination directory is set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_directory; (default log, relative to the data directory) and confirm it is the directory defined by your logging policy. Prefer an absolute path outside PGDATA (e.g. /var/log/postgres) so logs are not copied by pg_basebackup or pgBackRest.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_directory = '/var/log/postgres'; (create it owned by postgres, mode 0700) then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure the filename pattern for log files is set correctly
description: The log_filename setting specifies the filename pattern for log files. The value for log_filename should match your organization's logging policy. The value is treated as a strftime pattern, so %-escapes can be used to specify time- varying file names. The supported %-escapes are similar to those listed in the Open Group's strftime specification.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.5 Ensure the filename pattern for log files is set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_filename; (default postgresql-%a.log, one file per weekday) and confirm the strftime pattern matches your log retention and rotation policy.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_filename = 'postgresql-%Y%m%d.log'; then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure 'log_truncate_on_rotation' is enabled
description: Enabling the log_truncate_on_rotation setting when logging_collector is enabled causes PostgreSQL to truncate (overwrite) existing log files with the same name during log rotation instead of appending to them. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.7 Ensure 'log_truncate_on_rotation' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW log_truncate_on_rotation" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_truncate_on_rotation = 'on'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure the maximum log file lifetime is set correctly
description: When logging_collector is enabled, the log_rotation_age parameter determines the maximum lifetime of an individual log file (depending on the value of log_filename). After this many minutes have elapsed, a new log file will be created via automatic log file rotation.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.8 Ensure the maximum log file lifetime is set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_rotation_age; (default 1d) and confirm the value matches your logging policy for maximum log file lifetime.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_rotation_age = '1h'; (example) then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure the maximum log file size is set correctly
description: The log_rotation_size setting determines the maximum size of an individual log file. Once the maximum size is reached, automatic log file rotation will occur.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.9 Ensure the maximum log file size is set correctly

audit.command: Run SHOW log_rotation_size; (default 0, size-based rotation disabled) and confirm the value matches your logging policy.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_rotation_size = '1GB'; (example) then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure the correct syslog facility is selected
description: The syslog_facility setting specifies the syslog "facility" to be used when logging to syslog is enabled. You can choose from any of the 'local' facilities: ; LOCAL0 ; LOCAL1 ; LOCAL2 ; LOCAL3 ; LOCAL4 ; LOCAL5 ; LOCAL6 ; LOCAL7 Your organization's logging policy should dictate which facility to use based on the syslog daemon in use.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.10 Ensure the correct syslog facility is selected

audit.command: If logging to syslog, run SHOW syslog_facility; (default local0) and confirm it is the facility your syslog policy assigns to PostgreSQL (LOCAL0-LOCAL7).

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET syslog_facility = 'LOCAL1'; (example) then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure syslog messages are not suppressed
description: When logging to Syslog and syslog_sequence_numbers is on, then each message will be prefixed by an increasing sequence number (such as [2]). Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.11 Ensure syslog messages are not suppressed

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW syslog_sequence_numbers" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET syslog_sequence_numbers = 'on'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure syslog messages are not lost due to size
description: PostgreSQL log messages can exceed 1024 bytes, which is a typical size limit for traditional Syslog implementations. When syslog_split_messages is off, PostgreSQL server log messages are delivered to the Syslog service as is, and it is up to the Syslog service to cope with the potentially bulky messages. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.12 Ensure syslog messages are not lost due to size

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW syslog_split_messages" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET syslog_split_messages = 'on'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure the program name for PostgreSQL syslog messages is correct
description: The syslog_ident setting specifies the program name used to identify PostgreSQL messages in syslog logs. An example of a possible program name is postgres.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.13 Ensure the program name for PostgreSQL syslog messages is correct

audit.command: If logging to syslog, run SHOW syslog_ident; (default postgres) and confirm the program name matches your logging policy so messages from this cluster can be identified.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET syslog_ident = 'proddb'; (example) then SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure 'debug_print_parse' is disabled
description: The debug_print_parse setting enables printing the resulting parse tree for each executed query. These messages are emitted at the LOG message level. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, it is recommended this setting be disabled by setting it to off. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.16 Ensure 'debug_print_parse' is disabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW debug_print_parse" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET debug_print_parse = 'off'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'debug_print_rewritten' is disabled
description: The debug_print_rewritten setting enables printing the query rewriter output for each executed query. These messages are emitted at the LOG message level. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, it is recommended this setting be disabled by setting it to off. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.17 Ensure 'debug_print_rewritten' is disabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW debug_print_rewritten" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET debug_print_rewritten = 'off'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'debug_print_plan' is disabled
description: The debug_print_plan setting enables printing the execution plan for each executed query. These messages are emitted at the LOG message level. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, it is recommended this setting be disabled by setting it to off. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.18 Ensure 'debug_print_plan' is disabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW debug_print_plan" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET debug_print_plan = 'off'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'debug_pretty_print' is enabled
description: Enabling debug_pretty_print indents the messages produced by debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten, or debug_print_plan making them significantly easier to read. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.19 Ensure 'debug_pretty_print' is enabled

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW debug_pretty_print" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET debug_pretty_print = 'on'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_error_verbosity' is set correctly
description: The log_error_verbosity setting specifies the verbosity (amount of detail) of logged messages. Valid values are: ; TERSE ; DEFAULT ; VERBOSE with each containing the fields of the level above it as well as additional fields. TERSE excludes the logging of DETAIL, HINT, QUERY, and CONTEXT error information. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.22 Ensure 'log_error_verbosity' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW log_error_verbosity" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_error_verbosity = 'verbose'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_hostname' is set correctly
description: Enabling the log_hostname setting causes the hostname of the connecting host to be logged in addition to the host's IP address for connection log messages. Disabling the setting causes only the connecting host's IP address to be logged, and not the hostname. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.23 Ensure 'log_hostname' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SHOW log_hostname" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_hostname = 'off'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure 'log_timezone' is set correctly
description: The log_timezone setting specifies the time zone to use in timestamps within log messages. This value is cluster-wide, so that all sessions will report timestamps consistently. Unless directed otherwise by your organization's logging policy, set this to either GMT or UTC. Expects GMT/UTC; if your policy mandates another zone, accept this finding as an exception. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1.26 Ensure 'log_timezone' is set correctly

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT CASE WHEN current_setting('log_timezone') IN ('GMT','UTC','Etc/UTC','Etc/GMT') THEN 'compliant' ELSE 'noncompliant' END" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET log_timezone = 'GMT'" -c "SELECT pg_reload_conf()"

title: Ensure per-account connection limits are used
description: Limiting concurrent connections to a PostgreSQL server can be used to reduce the risk of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. Counts login roles with an unlimited (-1) connection limit. Runs psql as ${PGUSER:-postgres} against ${PGDATABASE:-postgres}; set PGHOST/PGPORT and use ~/.pgpass (not PGPASSWORD, see 1.6/1.7) when peer authentication is not available.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5 Ensure per-account connection limits are used

audit.command: out=$(psql -X -U "${PGUSER:-postgres}" -d "${PGDATABASE:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname !~ '^pg_' AND rolcanlogin AND rolconnlimit = -1" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out"

remediation.command: ALTER ROLE <dbuser> CONNECTION LIMIT <reasonable concurrent connection count>; for every login role reported (SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolconnlimit = -1).

title: Understanding attack vectors and runtime parameters
description: Understanding the vulnerability of PostgreSQL runtime parameters by the particular delivery method, or attack vector.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Understanding attack vectors and runtime parameters

audit.command: Review all configuration settings (SELECT name, setting, source, context FROM pg_settings ORDER BY context, name;) and the files postgresql.conf, postgresql.auto.conf and pg_hba.conf, and confirm logging records all modifications and changes to the RDBMS.

remediation.command: Keep configuration files under change control, restrict who can write them (postgres only), and enable logging/auditing (3.1.x, 3.2) so parameter changes are recorded.

title: Ensure 'Postmaster' Runtime Parameters are Configured
description: PostgreSQL runtime parameters that are executed by the postmaster process.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure 'Postmaster' Runtime Parameters are Configured

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE context = 'postmaster' ORDER BY 1; and compare with your approved baseline and with postgresql.conf/postgresql.auto.conf and $PGDATA/postmaster.opts. Any unexpected change is a fail.

remediation.command: Restore approved values in the configuration files and restart PostgreSQL (a full stop/start if the value came from the pg_ctl command line).

title: Ensure 'SIGHUP' Runtime Parameters are Configured
description: PostgreSQL runtime parameters that are executed by the SIGHUP signal.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4 Ensure 'SIGHUP' Runtime Parameters are Configured

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE context = 'sighup' ORDER BY 1; and compare with your approved baseline and the configuration files. Any unexpected value is a fail.

remediation.command: Restore approved values in postgresql.conf/postgresql.auto.conf and run SELECT pg_reload_conf(); (or send SIGHUP to the postmaster).

title: Ensure 'Superuser' Runtime Parameters are Configured
description: PostgreSQL runtime parameters that can only be executed by the server's superuser, postgres.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5 Ensure 'Superuser' Runtime Parameters are Configured

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE context = 'superuser' ORDER BY 1; and compare with your approved baseline; also check per-role/database overrides (SELECT * FROM pg_db_role_setting;). Any unexpected value is a fail.

remediation.command: Restore approved values in the configuration files (reload), and remove unwanted overrides with ALTER ROLE/ALTER DATABASE ... RESET <parameter>;

title: Ensure 'User' Runtime Parameters are Configured
description: These PostgreSQL runtime parameters are managed at the user account (ROLE) level.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.6 Ensure 'User' Runtime Parameters are Configured

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE context = 'user' ORDER BY 1; and inspect role and database overrides (SELECT * FROM pg_db_role_setting; \drds). Any value that differs from your approved baseline is a fail.

remediation.command: Reset unauthorized overrides with ALTER ROLE <role> [IN DATABASE <db>] RESET <parameter>; or ALTER DATABASE <db> RESET <parameter>; and correct the configuration files.

title: Ensure the pgcrypto extension is installed and configured correctly
description: PostgreSQL must implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure or modification of organization-defined information at rest (to include, at a minimum, PII and classified information) on organization-defined information system components.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.11 Ensure the pgcrypto extension is installed and configured correctly

audit.command: Run SELECT * FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'pgcrypto'; If data requires encryption and pgcrypto is not available/installed (installed_version empty), this is a fail. If disk or filesystem encryption is required, have the owners demonstrate it.

remediation.command: Install the contrib package if needed and run CREATE EXTENSION pgcrypto; in the databases that store data requiring column-level encryption; keep keys outside the database.

title: Ensure logging of replication commands is configured
description: Enabling the log_replication_commands setting causes each attempted replication from the server to be logged.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure logging of replication commands is configured

audit.command: Run SHOW log_replication_commands; If replication is used and the value is off, replication commands are not logged and this is a fail.

remediation.command: ALTER SYSTEM SET log_replication_commands = 'on'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();

title: Ensure PostgreSQL subdirectory locations are outside the data cluster
description: The PostgreSQL cluster is organized to carry out specific tasks in subdirectories. For the purposes of performance, reliability, and security some of these subdirectories should be relocated outside the data cluster.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.1 Ensure PostgreSQL subdirectory locations are outside the data cluster

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name ~ '_directory$' OR name ~ '_tablespace'; and inspect the returned paths: log/stats/temp/tablespace locations should be outside the data cluster and only superusers and authorized users may access them.

remediation.command: Relocate log_directory, tablespaces and other subdirectories outside PGDATA, owned by postgres with mode 0700, and update postgresql.conf accordingly.

title: Ensure the backup and restore tool, 'pgBackRest', is installed and configured
description: pgBackRest aims to be a simple, reliable backup and restore system that can seamlessly scale up to the largest databases and workloads. Instead of relying on traditional backup tools like tar and rsync, pgBackRest implements all backup features internally and uses a custom protocol for communicating with remote systems. Passes when the pgbackrest binary is installed and /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf (or /etc/pgbackrest.conf) exists; an alternative backup tool makes this an accepted exception.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.2 Ensure the backup and restore tool, 'pgBackRest', is installed and configured

audit.command: command -v pgbackrest >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo not-installed; exit 0; }; if [ -f /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf ] || [ -f /etc/pgbackrest.conf ]; then echo compliant; else echo not-configured; fi

remediation.command: Install pgBackRest from PGDG (dnf install pgbackrest / apt install pgbackrest), configure /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf (stanza, repository on separate storage, retention, logging), run pgbackrest --stanza=<name> stanza-create and test a restore.

title: Ensure miscellaneous configuration settings are correct
description: This recommendation covers non-regular, special files, and dynamic libraries. PostgreSQL permits local logins via the UNIX DOMAIN SOCKET and, for the most part, anyone with a legitimate Unix login account can make the attempt. Limiting PostgreSQL login attempts can be made by relocating the UNIX DOMAIN SOCKET to a subdirectory with restricted permissions.
reference: CIS PostgreSQL 18 Benchmark v1.0.0 - 8.3 Ensure miscellaneous configuration settings are correct

audit.command: Run SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('external_pid_file','unix_socket_directories','shared_preload_libraries','dynamic_library_path','local_preload_libraries','session_preload_libraries'); and confirm each value is expected and the referenced files/directories are writable only by postgres/root.

remediation.command: Correct unexpected values in postgresql.conf, restrict permissions on the referenced paths, and restart PostgreSQL.
